articles.title: Code Variables & Recipes
articles.summary: Sandboxed JavaScript expressions inside templates and campaign conditions — with prebuilt recipes for the common cases.

advanced.text: When a built-in variable or signal isn't enough, a code variable runs JavaScript in a guarded sandbox. You author it in a real code editor (syntax highlighting, helper autocomplete); the function receives three arguments and must return a string:

rows: The extracted page data — order.status, order.items[], contact.firstName, account.ytdRevenue…
Previously-resolved variables, so later code can build on earlier values (vars.order_number)
Query the live page: first element, all elements, or the first match's text
Fetch a page or JSON through the background worker (CORS-safe, allow-listed hosts)
Search the gift catalog by name similarity — top matches, or the single best one
Format values for the email ($1,234.00 · 1,234 · MM/DD/YYYY)
Extract a number, parse a date, format a phone as (###) ###-####

items: Async is automatic — write 'await' and the variable runs on the async path with a 10-second timeout.
Blocked outright: fetch(, chrome., eval(, import(, Function(, setTimeout/setInterval, Worker, XMLHttpRequest, and infinite-loop shapes like while(true). Use the h.* equivalents instead.
Bodies are capped at 8,192 characters. Errors surface in the variable table so you can fix them — at send time an erroring variable resolves to empty.

rows: Scans the order page for items flagged OOS — fully self-contained, sync
For each OOS item, fetches the brand's catalog and scores candidates by name/price/decoration to suggest the closest in-stock match (async)

advanced.text: Code variables run per-contact during campaigns and bulk sends. An expression that fetches pages adds those seconds for every contact in the audience — keep them lean.

articles.title: Console Commands
articles.summary: Two admin command objects available in the Settings page console: __gbSecret (hidden settings) and __gbScan (recent-orders scan clock).

advanced.text: Open DevTools on the Settings/editor page. Two helper objects are installed:

rows: Hide setting(s) from the Settings UI — values keep working, the switch disappears
Hide the entire Developer Settings section AND reset dev values to defaults
Bring the Developer Settings section back
Show when the recent-orders scan last ran
Clear the scan clock — the next scan covers the last 7 days

advanced.text: There is deliberately no UI for these. Hidden settings are how an admin locks a feature on or off for a teammate's profile — document what you hide, or future-you will file the bug.

articles.title: The Modal Playground
articles.summary: Every modal rendered with mock data outside the CRM — for trying features, demos, and design checks.

advanced.text: Developer Settings → 'Modal playground: Open' launches a standalone page where every modal renders with mock data — no CRM page, no live endpoints. Use it to explore a feature safely, demo the extension, or check how a theme variant looks across every surface.
The playground has its own CSS reset, so a layout that's fine there can still be off inside the CRM (host-page styles bleed into real modals). Verify real layouts on a real CRM page.

articles.title: Hidden Settings
articles.summary: How admins lock a feature on/off and remove its switch from the Settings UI — and how to see what's hidden.

advanced.text: A hidden setting keeps its value but loses its switch: the feature stays in whatever state the admin set, and the toggle no longer appears in Settings. It's a soft lock for keeping team configurations consistent.

items: Hide/show is console-only by design: __gbSecret.hide('taskListEnabled') etc. — see Console Commands.
Hidden state travels in presets via the 'Hidden-setting config' scope, so an admin can distribute locks with the team preset.

articles.title: Debug Storage Keys
articles.summary: Where the extension keeps its state, and which keys hold debug snapshots when you're chasing a problem.

advanced.text: All state lives in chrome.storage.local (inspect via the service-worker console: chrome.storage.local.get(null)). Useful keys when debugging:

rows: The latest variable-resolution snapshot — what each {{variable}} resolved to and from where
Per-recipient logs from the last bulk email run
The data caches (catalog, product config, inventory, costs)

advanced.text: Contact search speed comes from an IndexedDB database (gb-crm-index) — visible under DevTools → Application → IndexedDB.
Deleting cache keys is safe (they rebuild). Deleting templates, featureFlags, or devSettings is not — export a preset first if you're going to experiment.
